prize_parts.citation: For the design of pH-switchable ionizable lipids and their controlled self-assembly into nanoparticles, which made nucleic-acid medicines deliverable in vivo

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged in ballot, and I have settled the cut that I left open in round 1: Cullis, Hope and Madden. The scientific case rests on one identifiable concept that can be stated in a sentence: a lipid whose headgroup charge is switched by pH is near-neutral in circulation and cationic in the endosome, where it promotes a non-bilayer, membrane-destabilising phase, and rapid controlled mixing makes the lipid and nucleic acid co-assemble into small, efficiently loaded particles. That is lipid polymorphism and phase behaviour applied as design, it has been confirmed independently in approved siRNA and mRNA products, and it is mature. The 2023 Medicine prize honoured the nucleoside-modified cargo, not the carrier, so the chemistry of delivery is still unrecognised. Having read the whole exchange, B064 is also the configuration where the chair's question about the three-person cut has an answer I can defend on documented concept priority rather than on field loyalty.
statement.case_against: Credit is still the weak point: Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan made real contributions (lipidoid screening, the optimised clinical lipids, early siRNA formulations) and are excluded by any three-person line, which some colleagues will read as arbitrary. The disciplinary objection that this is pharmaceutical formulation next to the 2023 Medicine prize has not been fully answered by me, only argued. And B024 has three explicit supporters and cleaner attribution than anything I propose, so a vote for B064 accepts a messier citation for a more consequential one.

responses.point: Aili keeps Cullis, Hope and Madden, explains why Anderson is the most defensible alternative but still falls outside the line, and accepts my physical-chemistry framing as the answer to the formulation objection.
responses.response: I have moved to your trio. In round 1 I paired Cullis with Anderson, and your argument persuades me: the ionizable-lipid pKa principle and the rapid-mixing encapsulation concept are Vancouver work, and Madden's loading and mixing work is central to the encapsulation step, whereas lipidoid libraries optimised potency afterwards. I would keep your caveat in the citation text so the committee is explicit that this is a concept-priority cut, and not a ranking of who contributed most to the clinical products. I disagree only on how hard the disciplinary risk can be dismissed; we must expect it to be raised again.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, ranks B024 first for its clean two-person credit and forty years of use, and in his own uncertainties notes that Car-Parrinello is partly displaced in practice by Born-Oppenheimer MD and machine-learned potentials and that the category is contestable.
responses.response: I accept that B024 is the cleanest attribution on the list and I will not claim otherwise; I treat it as my second alternative. The point you raise yourself, that the citation must honour a 1985 conceptual step and not today's tools, is the point on which I remain unmoved: a prize for a unifying idea whose daily practice has largely moved to other schemes asks the committee to look backwards, whereas B064 recognises a design principle whose consequences are still unfolding. I also do not think the 2013 and 2024 computational prizes make B024 redundant, but they weaken its claim to be the chemistry-wide signal this year.

responses.point: Aqvist argues by a 'game-changer with shown consequences' standard that Car-Parrinello is the stronger case than folding theory or phase separation, and doubts that in vivo phase-separation evidence matches the in vitro droplet work.
responses.response: On phase separation you are right, and that is why B025 is no longer my configuration; I had already ranked B064 above it and your point confirms the judgement. But your own standard of demonstrated consequence favours B064 at least as much as B024: patisiran and the mRNA vaccines are four-decade-old lipid concepts verified in people, while Car-Parrinello's consequences are in computed understanding. I would like to hear whether you would, under that standard, accept B064 over B046 if the committee cannot agree on B024.

responses.point: Chabes prefers B012 with Balasubramanian and Klenerman, concedes that credit among Solexa, 454, Columbia terminators and clonal arrays is its weak point, and names B024 as the fallback if attribution cannot be settled.
responses.response: Your fallback shows the same instinct I have: the chemistry has to have a single decisive concept. I take your point that the reversible-terminator and cleavable-fluorophore chemistry in the Solexa route is real and unambiguously chemical, and I withdraw my round-1 phrase 'incremental' as too dismissive. My remaining concern is the one you raise: with several competing routes and the 1980 Sanger and Gilbert precedent, a two-person citation will be argued over, and B064 has, I think, a narrower dispute, because its argument is about where to stop in one group of collaborators rather than about which of several technologies won.

responses.point: Brzezinski, as Secretary, moved to B024 because a single dated, attributable discovery is easier to defend in the expert report, while conceding it lies close to condensed-matter physics and has no experimental or biological counterpart.
responses.response: The defensibility of the expert report is a fair weight and I do not dismiss it. I would say that B064 can be written as one dated concept too: the pKa-tuned ionizable lipid with controlled-mixing assembly, with the Vancouver papers as the documented record. Your own remark that B024 offers less chemistry-wide signal because it has no experimental counterpart is the reason I still weigh B064 higher: it bridges a physical-chemical principle to an experimental, clinically validated outcome.

uncertainties: Whether a majority accepts the lipid-delivery concept as core chemistry after the 2023 Medicine prize; I regard this as a judgement the committee must make, not a fact I can establish.

The three-person cut rests on my recollection of priority among the Vancouver and MIT groups; I have not verified the dates or the patent record, and MacLachlan's role in particular remains uncertain to me.

Whether the committee would prefer B024's cleaner credit even if it considers the category secondary, and whether B046 can reach a settled laureate list; I would move to B046 if its credit were settled and the clinical maturity concern eased.
statement.conflict_note: Updated: I work on lipid self-assembly and membrane phase behaviour, which is scientifically close to B064, and I have discounted for that by moving away from my own field's B025 in round 1 and by checking the concept-priority argument against Aili's. I have no personal collaboration or institutional tie with Cullis, Hope, Madden, Anderson, Langer or MacLachlan that I can identify from my profile, and I do not request recusal. I share Lund with Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, which has no bearing on B064. Colleagues should still weigh my enthusiasm accordingly.
